summary: Interleaved cache-window metering causing micro-charge lines and invoice proration discrepancy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports multiple small invoice line items (0.01-0.15 USD) across three hourly invoices after a rollout of a cache-window tuning change on 2026-03-09. Impact: Unexpected charges and incorrect prorating causing finance hold on their monthly payment (Invoice INV-2026-03-09-A).

Timeline:
- 2026-03-09 02:10 UTC: Cache-window tuning (PR #4821) deployed to prod/us-east (canary then full).
- 2026-03-09 03:30-05:00 UTC: Acme Health runs high volume chat traffic against open-llama-13b.
- 2026-03-10: Customer receives invoice showing micro-charge lines and an aggregated prorate misalignment across regional lines.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use an enterprise API key for Acme Health (redacted).
2) Run short streaming generation traffic (many short completions, average 8 tokens) against open-llama-13b with KV-cache enabled.
3) Trigger cache-eviction pattern (many interleaved prefixes) to exercise prefix/KV window behavior.

Observed behavior: Metering records many small usage rows for the same request window; biller service aggregates into separate invoice line items instead of coalescing into hourly buckets. Expected behavior: Metering should coalesce per-hour per-model usage and apply reserved/prorated rates; small internal cache-window bookkeeping entries should not surface to invoice line items.

Additional context: Customer flagged via #support-billing and held payment pending audit. Invoice: INV-2026-03-09-A. Meter job id: MJ-94471. Customer provided CSV of lines and a screenshot of invoice PDF. They are concerned about both the UX of line items and the net amount that was prorated across EUR conversion.
investigation_notes: 03-10 09:00 SPT: Confirmed PR 4821 adjusted KV cache window behavior to more aggressive short-prefix flushes (canary -> prod).

03-10 10:15 SRE: Metering pipeline shows multiple micro-entries for same request_id when prefix eviction triggered during streaming. Aggregate job (MJ-94471) did not collapse these entries due to new cache-window tag field mismatch.
03-10 11:00 Billing: Aggregation job (hourly_coalesce_v2) uses 'cache_tag' to group; new entries introduced 'cache_tag_v2' so they were treated as distinct buckets.

03-10 12:30 Finance: Proration routine applied regional conversion twice for a subset of lines (us-east -> EUR) due to duplicate mapping in hourly_coalesce_v2 output. Affected invoice lines show repeated prorate factor.

03-11 08:00 Findings: Root cause chain: PR 4821 changed cache metadata key names; metering encoders produced entries with both legacy and new keys during rollout overlap; coalescer only matched on exact keys leading to fragmented lines.
resolution: 2026-03-12: Applied provisional credit to Acme Health for the disputed amount (USD 187.34) and marked invoice INV-2026-03-09-A as 'under review' in billing portal.
2026-03-12: Hotfix deployed to hourly_coalesce_v2 to accept both legacy and new cache_tag names while we complete a cleanup job (PR 4867).
Planned follow-up: Run a backfill aggregation to collapse fragmented rows for MJ-94471 and re-emit corrected invoice lines; target completion 2026-03-15.
Long-term: Add rollout checklist item to ensure metering key renames include backward compatibility shim and end-to-end billing integration smoke test. Owner: Billing Engineering.
